quick_overview.quick_verdict: Kadence is a powerful, fast, and highly customizable theme with an exceptionally feature-rich free version. However, its extensive options create a steep learning curve for non-developers, and there are significant, documented compatibility issues with popular plugins like WPML and WooCommerce. While the Kadence theme core itself has a clean CVE history, the bundled Kadence Blocks plugin has seen two Contributor-level security disclosures in early 2026 (CVE-2026-1857 SSRF, CVE-2026-2633 Missing Authorization) — both at a time of ongoing vendor transition under StellarWP ownership, where patch-version transparency has not always matched Wordfence advisory pace. Of the 14 pain points identified, 4 affect the theme directly, while 10 relate to companion plugins, broader ecosystem integrations, or security exposure in bundled components.

community_pain_points_additions.title: Kadence Blocks: Server-Side Request Forgery via GetResponse API handler (CVE-2026-1857)
community_pain_points_additions.description: Disclosed February 2026. The Gutenberg Blocks with AI by Kadence WP plugin (Kadence Blocks) contains an SSRF vulnerability affecting all versions up to and including 3.6.1. Authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access can cause the site to make server-side requests to arbitrary endpoints on the configured GetResponse API server, exposing contact and campaign data and potentially leaking the stored API key in request headers. CWE-918. Root cause: insufficient endpoint parameter validation combined with an overly permissive permission check. As of disclosure, the CVE entry did not specify a fixed version — sites depending on the GetResponse integration should monitor for an explicit patch release and consider disabling the integration in the interim.
community_pain_points_additions.resolution: Update Kadence Blocks beyond 3.6.1 once an explicit fix is published; restrict Contributor-level users; remove GetResponse API key if integration is unused.

community_pain_points_additions.title: Kadence Blocks: Missing Authorization allows Contributor-level remote image uploads (CVE-2026-2633)
community_pain_points_additions.description: Disclosed February 2026. The process_image_data_ajax_callback() function in Kadence Blocks (up to and including 3.5.32) contains an incomplete capability check, allowing authenticated Contributor-level users to upload images from remote URLs into the WordPress Media Library — bypassing the normal WordPress role restrictions. CWE-862. Impact is bounded (no confidentiality or availability impact, low integrity impact via Media Library pollution), but the issue compounds with CVE-2026-1857 to establish a pattern: Contributor-level role surface in Kadence Blocks needs explicit review on multi-author sites.
community_pain_points_additions.resolution: Update Kadence Blocks beyond the patched version; audit Contributor accounts; consider role hardening.

community_pain_points_additions.title: Kadence security profile: clean theme core, Contributor-level surface in Kadence Blocks
community_pain_points_additions.description: Kadence theme core itself has a notably clean CVE history relative to its ~400K install base — no significant disclosures in 2025-2026. The exposure sits in the bundled Kadence Blocks plugin, where two Contributor-level vulnerabilities were disclosed within weeks of each other in February 2026. The pattern is consistent with the plugin's larger surface area (block library, AJAX handlers, third-party API integrations) rather than systemic vendor negligence. Context worth noting: this period overlaps with Kadence's transition under StellarWP/Liquid Web ownership and the departure of original founder Ben Ritner; patch-version disclosure clarity has been weaker than in the Brainstorm Force (Astra) comparison case, which is a soft signal worth monitoring rather than a current alarm.
community_pain_points_additions.resolution: Maintain Kadence Blocks updates within a defined window; monitor Wordfence Intelligence feed; review Contributor-role permissions.

scenario_updates.updates_verdict_caution: Exercise extreme caution when updating Kadence or its companion plugins on a live website, as there are multiple community reports of updates causing fatal errors or breaking block functionality [12, 14, 16]. The February 2026 Kadence Blocks CVEs (CVE-2026-1857, CVE-2026-2633) add an inverse pressure: delaying updates leaves Contributor-level attack surface exposed, so the staging workflow must be paired with active CVE monitoring rather than indefinite update postponement [26, 27].
scenario_updates.updates_recommendation: Kadence is updated very frequently, which is positive for security and features. However, due to the history of breaking changes [11, 12], a staging server is non-negotiable for testing all theme and plugin updates. Combine this with active Wordfence Intelligence (or equivalent) monitoring — the February 2026 Kadence Blocks disclosures illustrate that the bundled plugin surface, not the core theme, is where the current security pressure sits.

handoff_difficulty.handoff_verdict_caution: Use caution when handing off a Kadence-built site to non-technical clients, as the extensive customizer options and block-based workflow can be overwhelming compared to simpler themes or page builders [18, 21]. Additionally, multi-author sites granting Contributor-level access should review the role-based surface in Kadence Blocks given the February 2026 CVE disclosures [26, 27].

faq_items_additions.faq_question: Are there any known security vulnerabilities in Kadence?
faq_items_additions.faq_answer: The Kadence theme core itself has a clean recent CVE history. However, the bundled Kadence Blocks plugin had two Contributor-level vulnerabilities disclosed in February 2026: CVE-2026-1857 (SSRF in the GetResponse API handler, affecting versions ≤ 3.6.1) and CVE-2026-2633 (Missing Authorization in remote image upload, affecting versions ≤ 3.5.32). Both require an authenticated Contributor account, so multi-author sites should pay particular attention. Keep Kadence Blocks updated and monitor Wordfence advisories for explicit patched-version confirmations [26, 27].
